chunks: 1 - He said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Khalid al-Maraghi reported to me, he said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Bazzaz narrated to us, he said: Abu Abd Allah Ja'far ibn Abd Allah al-Alawi al-Muhammadi narrated to me, he said: Yahya ibn Hashim al-Ghassani narrated to us, from Abu Asim al-Nabil, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Alqamah ibn Qays, from Nawf al-Bikali, who said:

I spent a night with the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, and I saw him frequently going back and forth from his house and looking toward the sky. Then he entered as he would sometimes enter, and said: 'Are you sleeping or are you watching?' I said: 'Rather, I am watching, O Commander of the Faithful. I have not ceased observing you since tonight with my eyes, watching what you do.'

He said: 'O Nawf, blessed are those who renounce this world and desire the hereafter — a people who take the earth of God as their carpet, its dust as their cushion, His Book as their undergarment, supplication as their outer cover, and His water as their perfume. They renounce the world entirely, following the way of the Messiah, peace be upon him.'

Indeed, God the Exalted revealed to Jesus, peace be upon him: 'O Jesus, you must follow the first path so that you may join the ranks of the messengers. Say to your people, O brother of the warners: Do not enter any of My houses except with pure hearts, clean hands, and humble eyes. For indeed I do not hear from any supplicant who calls upon Me while any of My servants has an unresolved injustice against him, and I do not answer his prayer while I have a right from him that he has not returned to Me.'
So if you are able, O Nawf, to not be a monitor, a poet, a drummer, or a lute player, then do so.

For indeed David, peace be upon him, the messenger of the Lord of the worlds, went out one night and looked at the parts of the sky, then said: By God, Lord of David, this is indeed an hour in which no Muslim servant asks God for good during it except that He grants it to him — unless he is a monitor, a poet, a drummer, or a lute player.'

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib, the first Shia Imam and fourth Rashidun caliph
key_terms.الدُّعاء: Personal prayer and invocation directed to God
key_terms.الزُّهد: Spiritual practice of detaching from worldly pleasures to focus on the hereafter
key_terms.قيام الليل: Voluntary prayer performed in the last third of the night, highly recommended in Islam

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali teach about asceticism and the conditions for accepted prayer?
ai.summary: In this night-time teaching, Imam Ali (AS) addresses his companion Nawf al-Bikali, who had been watching the Imam's devotions throughout the night. Ali describes the blessed qualities of ascetics who renounce worldly attachments and follow the path of Prophet Jesus (AS). He then recounts a divine revelation to Jesus, wherein God sets conditions for those who wish their prayers to be heard in His houses of worship: purity of heart, cleanliness of hands, and humility of sight. God declares He will not answer the prayer of one who harbors an injustice against others. Ali concludes by advising Nawf to avoid certain occupations — monitor (tax collector), poet (of vanity), drummer, and lute player — citing Prophet David's (AS) account of a blessed hour of the night when prayers are answered, except for those in such roles.
